To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
24-hour AP and HR, but not the office AP and HR or the maximal AP and HR during bicycle exercise, predict LVM.

1) the 24-hour AP is a more reliable index than office BP in predicting LVH; 2) the office HR and HR response to effort are also useful predictors of LVH; 3) the maximal AP response to effort does not predict LVH; 4) the LVH index correlates with office HR and HR at rest and during effort.

1) 24-hour AP and HR recordings are superior to office measurements in identifying hypertensive patients with LVH; and 2) 24-hour monitoring of AP and HR may be more useful than office measurements in identifying the hypertensive patients who are at risk of developing LVH.
